source.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.

records.literal_gloss: You heard that it was said, Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.

en.L: You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.'
en.B: You have heard the saying, 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth.'
en.R: You have heard that the law says, 'The punishment must match the harm: an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.'

es.L: {{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}} que se dijo: “Ojo por ojo y diente por diente”.
es.B: {{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}} el dicho: “Ojo por ojo, diente por diente”.
es.R: {{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}} que la ley dice: “El castigo tiene que ser igual al daño: ojo por ojo y diente por diente”.

fr.L: Vous avez entendu qu’il a été dit : “Œil pour œil et dent pour dent.”
fr.B: Vous avez entendu cette parole : “Œil pour œil, dent pour dent.”
fr.R: Vous avez entendu que la Loi dit : “La punition doit être égale au mal qu’on a fait : œil pour œil, dent pour dent.”

sw.L: Mlisikia kwamba ilisemwa, 'Jicho badala ya jicho, na jino badala ya jino.'
sw.B: Mmesikia msemo huu: 'Jicho kwa jicho, jino kwa jino.'
sw.R: Mmesikia kwamba sheria inasema, 'Adhabu lazima ilingane na madhara: jicho kwa jicho, na jino kwa jino.'

ko.L: 너희는 '눈은 눈으로, 이는 이로' 하신 말씀을 들었다.
ko.B: 너희는 '눈에는 눈, 이에는 이'라고 하신 말씀을 들었다.
ko.R: 너희는 율법에 '벌은 입힌 해만큼만 받아야 한다. 눈에는 눈, 이에는 이로 갚아라'라고 한 말을 들었다.

vi.L: Các con đã nghe có lời nói rằng: 'Mắt đền mắt và răng đền răng.'
vi.B: Các con đã nghe câu: 'Mắt đền mắt, răng đền răng.'
vi.R: Các con đã nghe luật pháp dạy: 'Hình phạt phải tương xứng với thiệt hại: mắt đền mắt, răng đền răng.'

pt.L: Vocês ouviram que foi dito: 'Olho por olho e dente por dente.'
pt.B: Vocês ouviram o ditado: 'Olho por olho, dente por dente.'
pt.R: Vocês ouviram que a Lei diz: 'O castigo deve ser igual ao dano: olho por olho e dente por dente.'

am.L: “በዓይን ፋንታ ዓይን፣ በጥርስም ፋንታ ጥርስ” እንደ ተባለ ሰምታችኋል።
am.B: “ዓይን ስለ ዓይን፣ ጥርስ ስለ ጥርስ” የሚለውን አባባል ሰምታችኋል።
am.R: ሕጉ “ቅጣቱ ከጉዳቱ ጋር እኩል ይሁን፤ ዓይን ስለ ዓይን፣ ጥርስም ስለ ጥርስ” እንደሚል ሰምታችኋል።

ru.L: Вы слышали, что было сказано: “Глаз за глаз и зуб за зуб.”
ru.B: Вы слышали изречение: “Глаз за глаз, зуб за зуб.”
ru.R: Вы слышали, что говорит Закон: “Наказание должно быть равно вреду: глаз за глаз и зуб за зуб.”

hi.L: तुमने सुना है कि कहा गया था, 'आँख के बदले आँख, और दाँत के बदले दाँत।'
hi.B: तुम यह कहावत सुन चुके हो, 'आँख के बदले आँख, दाँत के बदले दाँत।'
hi.R: तुमने सुना है कि व्यवस्था कहती है, 'सज़ा उतनी ही हो जितना नुक़सान हुआ: आँख के बदले आँख, और दाँत के बदले दाँत।'

uk.L: Ви чули, що сказано: “Око за око і зуб за зуб.”
uk.B: Ви чули вислів: “Око за око, зуб за зуб.”
uk.R: Ви чули, що Закон каже: “Покарання має відповідати шкоді: око за око і зуб за зуб.”

ja.L: あなたがたは、こう言われたと聞いている。『目には目を、歯には歯を。』
ja.B: あなたがたは、こう言い渡されたことを聞いている。『目には目を、歯には歯を。』
ja.R: あなたたちは、神の律法でこう教えられたことを聞いている。『罰は受けた害と同じでなければならない。目には目を、歯には歯を。』

decisions.choice: eye for eye: the law of equal justice (Exodus 21:24; Leviticus 24:20; Deuteronomy 19:21)
decisions.reason: The law set a limit for judges: the penalty must match the harm and go no further. In practice it was often settled by payment. People could also take it as a right to pay back what they had suffered.

decisions.choice: The punishment must match the harm
decisions.reason: Readable says what the principle meant.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural 'you' ({{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}}, {{plural_you:les|os}}, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}})
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the crowd, so each plural "you", pronoun or verb, is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). Where he turns to one listener, as in verses 39-42, Spanish uses "tú", which has no setting. The same through verse 48.

decisions.choice: jicho badala ya jicho (L); jicho kwa jicho (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek preposition means "in place of". Literal shows it with "badala ya"; Balanced and Readable give the saying in its short Swahili form.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to his hearers in 해라체 with "너희" and "너", through Matthew 5:38-48; "하신 말씀" (L, B) where the saying is from the law
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Sermon on the Mount. The law of equal justice is God's law (meaning decision), so the passive "it was said" is rendered with the honorific "하신", as in 5:21, 5:27 and 5:33.

decisions.choice: 'Глаз за глаз'
decisions.reason: 'Око' is Church Slavonic; the saying reads in modern words at every level.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλ’ ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·

records.literal_gloss: I but say to you not to resist the evil [person]; but whoever you strikes on the right cheek, turn to him also the other;

en.L: But I say to you not to resist the evil [person]; but whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to {{gender:them|him}} as well,
en.B: But I tell you, do not fight back against an evil person. If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn the other cheek to {{gender:them|him}} as well.
en.R: But I tell you, do not fight back against someone who does wrong to you. If someone slaps you on the right side of your face, let them slap the other side too.

es.L: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que no {{plural_you:resistan|resistáis}} al malvado; sino que al que te abofetea en la mejilla derecha, preséntale también la otra.
es.B: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no le {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} frente al malvado. Si alguien te da una bofetada en la mejilla derecha, ofrécele también la otra.
es.R: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no {{plural_you:se desquiten|os desquitéis}} con quien {{plural_you:les|os}} hace daño. Si alguien te da una bofetada en el lado derecho de la cara, deja que te pegue también en el otro lado.

fr.L: Mais moi, je vous dis de ne pas vous opposer au méchant ; au contraire, quiconque te gifle sur la joue droite, tourne aussi vers lui l’autre ;
fr.B: Mais moi, je vous le dis : ne ripostez pas à celui qui vous fait du mal. Si quelqu’un te gifle sur la joue droite, tends-lui aussi l’autre joue.
fr.R: Mais moi, je vous le dis : ne rendez pas le mal à celui qui vous fait du tort. Si quelqu’un te gifle sur la joue droite, laisse-le te gifler aussi sur l’autre joue.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia msimpinge mwovu; badala yake, yeyote anayekupiga kofi kwenye shavu la kulia, umgeuzie pia lile lingine.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia, msimlipize kisasi mtu mwovu. Mtu akikupiga kofi kwenye shavu la kulia, mgeuzie na shavu lingine pia.
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia, msimlipize kisasi mtu anayewatendea mabaya. Mtu akikupiga kofi upande wa kulia wa uso wako, mwache akupige na upande mwingine pia.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 너희에게 말한다. 악한 [사람]에게 맞서지 마라. 오히려 누구든지 네 오른쪽 뺨을 치거든, 그에게 다른 [뺨]도 돌려 대어라.
ko.B: 그러나 나는 너희에게 말한다. 악한 사람에게 맞서 싸우지 마라. 누가 네 오른쪽 뺨을 때리거든, 그 사람에게 다른 쪽 뺨도 돌려 대어라.
ko.R: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 너에게 잘못하는 사람에게 앙갚음하지 마라. 누가 네 오른쪽 뺨을 때리면, 다른 쪽 뺨도 때리게 내버려 두어라.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, đừng chống cự kẻ ác; nhưng ai vả má bên phải của con, hãy đưa luôn má kia cho người ấy,
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, đừng chống trả người làm điều ác. Nếu ai tát má bên phải của con, hãy đưa luôn má bên kia cho người ấy.
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, đừng đánh trả người làm hại mình. Nếu có ai tát vào má phải của con, hãy để người ấy tát luôn má bên kia.

pt.L: Mas eu lhes digo que não resistam à [pessoa] má; mas, a quem bater em você na face direita, vire para ele também a outra;
pt.B: Mas eu lhes digo: não revidem contra quem é mau. Se alguém der um tapa na sua face direita, vire para ele também a outra face.
pt.R: Mas eu digo a vocês: não revidem quando alguém fizer mal a vocês. Se alguém der um tapa no lado direito do seu rosto, deixe essa pessoa bater também no outro lado.

am.L: እኔ ግን ክፉውን [ሰው] እንዳትቃወሙ እላችኋለሁ፤ ነገር ግን ማንም ቀኝ ጉንጭህን በጥፊ ቢመታህ ሌላውንም ደግሞ {{gender:ለዚያ ሰው|ለእርሱ}} አዙር፣
am.B: እኔ ግን እላችኋለሁ፣ በክፉ ሰው ላይ አጸፋ አትመልሱ። ማንም ቀኝ ጉንጭህን በጥፊ ቢመታህ ሌላውንም ጉንጭህን {{gender:ለዚያ ሰው|ለእርሱ}} አዙር።
am.R: እኔ ግን እነግራችኋለሁ፣ ክፉ ነገር ያደረገባችሁን ሰው መልሳችሁ አትዋጉት። አንድ ሰው ቀኝ ጉንጭህን በጥፊ ቢመታህ ሌላውንም ጉንጭህን እንዲመታ ፍቀድለት።

ru.L: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю вам не противиться злому [человеку]; но кто ударит тебя по правой щеке, обрати к нему и другую,
ru.B: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю вам: не давайте отпора злому человеку. Если кто-то ударит тебя по правой щеке, подставь ему и другую.
ru.R: Но {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю вам: не отвечайте злом тому, кто делает вам зло. Если кто-то даст тебе пощёчину по правой щеке, подставь и другую.

hi.L: पर मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ कि दुष्ट व्यक्ति का विरोध मत करो; बल्कि जो तुम्हारे दाहिने गाल पर थप्पड़ मारता है, उसकी ओर दूसरा [गाल] भी कर दो,
hi.B: पर मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ, बुरे व्यक्ति से बदला मत लो। यदि कोई तुम्हारे दाहिने गाल पर थप्पड़ मारे, तो उसकी ओर दूसरा गाल भी कर दो।
hi.R: पर मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ, जो तुम्हारे साथ बुरा करे, उससे बदला मत लो। अगर कोई तुम्हारे चेहरे के दाहिनी ओर थप्पड़ मारे, तो उसे दूसरी ओर भी मारने दो।

uk.L: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} кажу вам не противитися злому; але хто вдарить тебе по правій щоці, підстав йому й другу,
uk.B: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} кажу вам: не давайте відсічі лихій людині. Якщо хтось ударить тебе по правій щоці, підстав йому й другу.
uk.R: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} кажу вам: не мстіться тому, хто чинить вам зло. Якщо хтось дасть тобі ляпаса по правій щоці, дозволь йому вдарити й по лівій.

ja.L: しかしこのわたしは、あなたがたに言う。悪い者に立ち向かわないように。むしろ、あなたの右の頬を平手で打つ者がいれば、その人にもう一方の[頬]も向けなさい。
ja.B: しかし、わたしがあなたがたに言うのは、こうである。悪を行う者にやり返してはならない。だれかがあなたの右の頬を平手で打つなら、その人にもう一方の頬も差し出しなさい。
ja.R: でも、わたしはあなたたちにこう言う。あなたにひどいことをする人に、仕返しをしてはいけない。だれかがあなたの顔の右側をたたいたら、反対側もたたかせなさい。

decisions.choice: do not resist the evil person: do not pay back wrong with wrong
alternatives: never oppose evil in any way
decisions.reason: After "eye for eye", resisting means taking revenge or answering harm with harm. The examples are of insults and demands made on a person, not of standing by while others are harmed.

decisions.choice: slaps you on the right cheek: a backhanded slap, an insult
decisions.reason: A right-handed blow to the right cheek would be with the back of the hand, a gesture of contempt. The point is not to answer insult with insult.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The one who strikes may be anyone, so the inclusive form is the default. Readable uses "someone ... them", which already includes everyone.

decisions.choice: preséntale, ofrécele, deja que te pegue, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "them" with "him" as the traditional form. Spanish "le" and the verb ending serve for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change. The same in verses 40 and 41, where "con él" after "quien" is the ordinary pronoun for anyone.

decisions.choice: "quiconque", "quelqu'un" … "lui", "le" with no gender span, in 5:39-42
decisions.reason: Where the English needs {{gender:them|him}}, French "quiconque" and "quelqu'un" already mean anyone, and the "lui" that refers back to them is ordinary generic French (style guide §7), as in Luke 6:29.

decisions.choice: "vous" for the command, "tu" for the examples
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks to all the hearers and then, in 5:39b-42, to each one in the singular; French follows the Greek number (style guide §6), as Luke 6:29-30 does. "Gifler" says the slap of the Greek verb (m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}
decisions.reason: Jesus's emphatic "I" is a free pronoun in Swahili, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting as the Swahili style guide has it for "mimi", though English leaves "I" without one. The same in verse 44.

decisions.choice: umgeuzie, mwache, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "them" with "him" as the traditional form. Swahili marks the person inside the verb (-m-), which serves for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change. The same in verses 40 and 41.

decisions.choice: "그", "그 사람" with no gender span, through Matthew 5:39-41
decisions.reason: Korean "그 사람" and "누가" are neither male nor female, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Korean.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" with no gender span (also 5:40-41)
decisions.reason: "Người ấy" already means a man or a woman, so Vietnamese has no traditional form to set against it; the English {{gender:them|him}} has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "kẻ ác" (L); "người làm điều ác" (B); "người làm hại mình" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as the evil person who wrongs you; Literal keeps the word used in 5:37, and Balanced and Readable say who is meant.

decisions.choice: ele, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs "them|him". In Portuguese the "ele" that refers back to "quem" or "alguém" is ordinary generic Portuguese and includes women (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7), so no setting is needed here or in 5:40-41.

decisions.choice: não revidem
decisions.reason: As the meaning note says (m1), the sense is not paying back wrong with wrong; "revidar" says exactly that in Portuguese, where "resistir" could mean any refusal or self-defence. Literal keeps "resistir".

decisions.choice: {{gender:ለዚያ ሰው|ለእርሱ}} (to that person, or to him)
alternatives: an object suffix on the verb (አዙርለት)
decisions.reason: The one who strikes may be a man or a woman. Amharic pronouns are masculine or feminine, so the default says "that person" and the setting gives the traditional "him", as the English span does. A suffix on the verb would leave nothing for the setting to change. The same pattern is used in 5:40-41.

decisions.choice: "उसकी", "उसे" with no gender span
alternatives: a span with separate forms for a man and a woman
decisions.reason: The English offers "them" or "him". Hindi "वह", "उसकी", "उसे" serve for either sex, so there is nothing for a gender setting to change. This holds for the rest of the passage (5:40-41).

decisions.choice: 'ему' without a gender span
decisions.reason: The English has gender spans on 'them/him' in 5:39-41. In Russian 'ему' agrees with 'кто' and 'кто-то', which cover a man or a woman, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: "йому" with no gender span
decisions.reason: In Ukrainian the pronoun agrees with "хто" or "хтось", which already cover anyone, man or woman, so the English gender span on "him" is not needed here or in 5:40-41.

decisions.choice: "その人" with no gender span; the same in 5:40-42
decisions.reason: The English needs a them/him span for the one who strikes, sues or compels. Japanese "その人" or no pronoun covers anyone, so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: "平手で打つ"
decisions.reason: The verb is for a slap, a blow of insult rather than injury (m2).

source.text: καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·

records.literal_gloss: and to the [one] wanting you to sue and the tunic of you to take, let go to him also the cloak;

en.L: and to the one who wants to sue you and take your tunic, let {{gender:them|him}} have your cloak as well,
en.B: If someone wants to take you to court and take your shirt, let {{gender:them|him}} have your coat as well.
en.R: If someone takes you to court to get your shirt, give that person your coat too.

es.L: y al que quiere demandarte y tomar tu túnica, cédele también el manto;
es.B: Si alguien quiere ponerte una demanda para quitarte la camisa, deja que se lleve también el abrigo.
es.R: Si alguien te lleva ante el juez para quedarse con tu camisa, dale también tu abrigo.

fr.L: et à celui qui veut te faire un procès et prendre ta tunique, laisse-lui aussi le manteau ;
fr.B: Si quelqu’un veut te traîner en justice pour prendre ta chemise, laisse-lui aussi ton manteau.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un va au tribunal pour te prendre ta chemise, donne-lui aussi ton manteau.

sw.L: na yeye anayetaka kukushtaki ili achukue vazi lako la ndani, mwachilie pia vazi la nje;
sw.B: Mtu akitaka kukupeleka mahakamani ili achukue shati lako, mwache achukue na koti lako pia.

decisions.choice: tunic and cloak: the inner garment and the outer one
decisions.reason: The tunic was worn next to the skin; the cloak was the outer garment, also used as a blanket at night. The law did not let a creditor keep a poor man's cloak overnight (Exodus 22:26-27). Jesus tells his followers to give up even what the law protected.

decisions.choice: shirt, coat
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the nearest modern garments; Literal keeps the ancient names.

decisions.choice: vazi la ndani, vazi la nje (L); shati, koti (B, R)
decisions.reason: The inner garment and the outer one (meaning decision m1). "Kanzu" and "joho" are the familiar words, but "kanzu" today names a particular men's gown, so Literal describes the two garments and Balanced and Readable use the nearest modern ones, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "속옷", "겉옷" (L); "옷", "겉옷" (B); "입고 있는 옷", "외투" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the tunic worn next to the skin and the outer cloak (meaning decision). Literal keeps the pair "속옷/겉옷"; since "속옷" now means underwear, Balanced and Readable name the tunic as the clothes one wears.

decisions.choice: "áo trong", "áo ngoài" (L); "áo sơ mi", "áo khoác" (B); "áo", "áo khoác" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal names the inner and outer garments, as the meaning decision describes them; Balanced and Readable use the everyday clothes the English names.

decisions.choice: ቀሚስ ... ካባ (tunic ... cloak, L); ሸሚዝ ... ካባ (B); ሸሚዝ ... ኮት (shirt ... coat, R)
alternatives: እጀ ጠባብ ... መጎናጸፊያ (the old church words)
decisions.reason: The tunic was the long garment worn next to the body, the cloak the outer one a poor man also slept in. Literal names the old garments; Balanced and Readable use the everyday garments that stand in the same relation, as the English does.
The tunic was the inner garment, the cloak the outer one that also served as a blanket. Each level names a familiar pair of inner and outer clothes.

decisions.choice: 'хитон' (L); 'рубашка' (B, R)

decisions.choice: "肌着" / "外衣" (L); "肌着" / "外套" (B); "シャツ" / "コート" (R)
decisions.reason: The inner garment worn next to the skin and the outer one also used as a blanket (m1). Readable uses the nearest everyday clothes, as the English does.

decisions.choice: compels: forces you into service, as Roman soldiers could
decisions.reason: The verb is a borrowed word for official forced service. Soldiers and officials could make people carry loads, as Simon of Cyrene was made to carry the cross (27:32).

decisions.choice: mile: a Roman mile, a thousand paces, a little shorter than a modern mile
decisions.reason: The difference does not affect the saying.

decisions.choice: to carry a load (B); a soldier makes you carry something (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what was usually demanded; Readable names who usually demanded it. The Greek does not name the person.

decisions.choice: una milla, with no units span
decisions.reason: The Roman mile was a thousand paces, a little shorter than a modern mile (meaning decision m2). The English keeps "mile" with no units setting, and "milla" is a unit Spanish readers know, so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: un mille (L); {{units:un kilomètre et demi|un mille}} (B, R)
alternatives: un mille at every level, as the English
decisions.reason: The English keeps "mile" at every level because a Roman mile is close to an English one (m2). French readers measure in kilometres, so Balanced and Readable give the metric distance by default (a Roman mile was about 1.5 km) with the original unit as the alternative, as the style guide asks (§7). Literal keeps the original unit.

decisions.choice: maili moja, with no units span
decisions.reason: The Roman mile was a thousand paces, a little shorter than a modern mile (meaning decision m2). The English keeps "mile" with no units setting, and "maili" is a unit Swahili readers know, so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: {{units:1.5킬로미터를|1마일을}}, {{units:3킬로미터를|2마일을}} (B, R); "일 마일", "이 마일" (L)
decisions.reason: The Roman mile was a thousand paces, about one and a half kilometers (meaning decision). As docs/korean-style.md section 7 asks, the metric distance is the default and the original unit the alternative, which differs from the English (US miles, no span); the particle goes inside the spans because the two forms end differently. Literal keeps the original unit. "오 리" is the older Korean Bibles' rendering.

decisions.choice: {{units:1,5 km|một dặm}} and {{units:3 km|hai dặm}} (B, R); Literal keeps "một dặm"
decisions.reason: The style guide gives modern measures in metric by default in Vietnamese, with the original unit as the alternative; the English needs no span here because "mile" is already its modern unit. A Roman mile was about 1.5 km.

decisions.choice: milha, with no units setting
decisions.reason: Brazil measures in kilometres, but the Roman mile is the unit of the saying, and "a segunda milha" is how Brazilian readers know it; as the English, the exact length does not matter (m2), so no units setting is used.

decisions.choice: ማይል (a mile), with no units span
alternatives: ምዕራፍ (the old word for a stage of road)
decisions.reason: The Roman mile was about a kilometre and a half, but the point is the length a soldier could make you carry his load, which Jesus doubles. The English has no units span here, so neither does the Amharic; "ማይል" is understood, and a metric figure would make the saying a measurement.

decisions.choice: {{units:полтора километра|одну милю}}, {{units:три километра|две мили}}
alternatives: 'одну милю ... две' with no setting, as the English
decisions.reason: The English has no setting here because a Roman mile is close to an English one. Russian readers count in kilometres, so Balanced and Readable give the distance in metric by default (a Roman mile is about 1.5 km) and the mile as the alternative; Literal keeps the mile.

decisions.choice: "милю" with no units span
decisions.reason: The English keeps the mile without a setting, since the saying turns on one measured stage and then a second. A metric figure would blur the picture, so Ukrainian keeps "миля", which readers know as an old measure.

decisions.choice: {{units:約1.5キロメートル|一ミリオン}}, {{units:約3キロメートル|二ミリオン}}
alternatives: "一マイル" with no span, as the English
decisions.reason: The English can say mile with no span because a US mile is close to a Roman one (m2). Japanese readers count in kilometers, so Balanced and Readable give the distance in metric by default with the Roman mile as the alternative; Literal keeps ミリオン.

ja.L: あなたに願う者には与えなさい。また、あなたから借りたいと望む者から顔をそむけてはならない。
ja.B: 頼んでくる人にはだれにでも与えなさい。借りたいと言ってくる人を、追い返してはならない。
ja.R: 何かを求めてくる人には、だれにでもあげなさい。あなたから借りたいと言う人に、貸すのを断ってはいけない。

decisions.choice: give and lend: the generosity the law asked for (Deuteronomy 15:7-11)
alternatives: a rule to give whatever is asked
decisions.reason: The law told Israel to lend freely to the poor. Jesus's saying belongs with the others: a disciple does not hold on to his rights or his goods.

source.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: You heard that it was said, You will love the neighbor of you and will hate the enemy of you.

en.L: You have heard that it was said, 'You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
en.B: You have heard the saying, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
en.R: You have heard that people say, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'

es.B: {{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}} el dicho: “Ama a tu prójimo y odia a tu enemigo”.
es.R: {{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}} que la gente dice: “Ama a tu prójimo y odia a tu enemigo”.

fr.L: Vous avez entendu qu’il a été dit : “Tu aimeras ton prochain et tu haïras ton ennemi.”
fr.B: Vous avez entendu cette parole : “Aime ton prochain et déteste ton ennemi.”
fr.R: Vous avez entendu que les gens disent : “Aime ton prochain et déteste ton ennemi.”

sw.L: Mlisikia kwamba ilisemwa, 'Utampenda jirani yako na kumchukia adui yako.'
sw.B: Mmesikia msemo huu: 'Mpende jirani yako na umchukie adui yako.'
sw.R: Mmesikia watu wakisema, 'Mpende jirani yako, na umchukie adui yako.'

ko.L: 너희는 '네 이웃을 사랑하고 네 원수를 미워하여라'라고 한 말을 들었다.
ko.B: 너희는 '네 이웃을 사랑하고 네 원수를 미워하여라'라는 말을 들었다.
ko.R: 너희는 사람들이 '네 이웃을 사랑하고 네 원수를 미워하여라'라고 하는 말을 들었다.

vi.L: Các con đã nghe có lời nói rằng: 'Ngươi phải yêu thương người lân cận và ghét kẻ thù mình.'
vi.B: Các con đã nghe câu: 'Hãy yêu thương người lân cận và ghét kẻ thù mình.'
vi.R: Các con đã nghe người ta nói: 'Hãy yêu thương người gần gũi mình và ghét kẻ thù mình.'

pt.L: Vocês ouviram que foi dito: 'Amarás o teu próximo e odiarás o teu inimigo.'
pt.B: Vocês ouviram o ditado: 'Ama o teu próximo e odeia o teu inimigo.'
pt.R: Vocês ouviram o que as pessoas dizem: 'Ama o teu próximo e odeia o teu inimigo.'

am.L: “ባልንጀራህን ትወዳለህ፤ ጠላትህንም ትጠላለህ” እንደ ተባለ ሰምታችኋል።
am.B: “ባልንጀራህን ውደድ፤ ጠላትህን ጥላ” የሚለውን አባባል ሰምታችኋል።
am.R: ሰዎች “ባልንጀራህን ውደድ፤ ጠላትህን ጥላ” እንደሚሉ ሰምታችኋል።

ru.L: Вы слышали, что было сказано: “Возлюбишь ближнего твоего и возненавидишь врага твоего.”
ru.B: Вы слышали изречение: “Люби ближнего и ненавидь врага.”
ru.R: Вы слышали, что люди говорят: “Люби своего ближнего и ненавидь своего врага.”

hi.L: तुमने सुना है कि कहा गया था, 'अपने पड़ोसी से प्रेम करना और अपने शत्रु से बैर।'
hi.B: तुम यह कहावत सुन चुके हो, 'अपने पड़ोसी से प्रेम करो और अपने शत्रु से घृणा।'
hi.R: तुमने सुना है कि लोग कहते हैं, 'अपने पड़ोसी से प्रेम करो और अपने दुश्मन से नफ़रत करो।'

uk.L: Ви чули, що сказано: “Любитимеш свого ближнього і ненавидітимеш свого ворога.”
uk.B: Ви чули вислів: “Люби свого ближнього і ненавидь свого ворога.”
uk.R: Ви чули, як люди кажуть: “Люби свого ближнього і ненавидь свого ворога.”

ja.L: あなたがたは、こう言われたと聞いている。『あなたの隣人を愛し、あなたの敵を憎まなければならない。』
ja.B: あなたがたは、こう言い渡されたことを聞いている。『隣人を愛し、敵を憎みなさい。』
ja.R: あなたたちは、人々がこう言うのを聞いている。『隣人を愛しなさい。そして、敵を憎みなさい。』

decisions.choice: love your neighbor: Leviticus 19:18; hate your enemy: not in the law
alternatives: both halves are commands of the law
decisions.reason: The law commands love of neighbor. No law commands hatred of enemies, but it was drawn from the first command: if the neighbor is a fellow Israelite, the enemy is not. The Dead Sea Scrolls teach hatred of the "sons of darkness" (Rule of the Community 1.10).

decisions.choice: people say
decisions.reason: The second half is not in the law, so Readable does not say "the law says" here.

decisions.choice: "한 말", "라는 말" with no honorific, where 5:21-38 have "하신 말씀"
decisions.reason: "Hate your enemy" is not in the law (meaning decision), so Korean does not use the honorific that would make God its speaker.

decisions.choice: "người lân cận" (L, B); "người gần gũi mình" (R) for neighbor
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:31 for Literal and Balanced. Mark's Readable says "người khác", but here the neighbor is set against the enemy, so Readable says "người gần gũi mình", those close to you.

decisions.choice: o teu próximo
decisions.reason: "Próximo" is the Portuguese word for neighbour in the law's sense, the other person one lives among; "vizinho" would mean only the people next door. The saying keeps the "tu" of the commandment it quotes.

decisions.choice: ባልንጀራ (neighbor, fellow)
decisions.reason: The Greek word, from Leviticus 19:18, means the other person one lives among, not only the one next door. "ባልንጀራ" carries that wider sense; "ጎረቤት" would narrow it to a neighbor's house.

decisions.choice: "人々がこう言うのを聞いている" (R), not the formula's "神の律法でこう教えられた"
decisions.reason: Hatred of enemies is not in the law (m1), so Readable does not say the law teaches it, as the English Readable also changes its wording here.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: I but say to you, love the enemies of you and pray for the [ones] persecuting you;

en.L: But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
en.B: But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for the people who persecute you,
en.R: But I tell you, love your enemies. Pray for the people who hurt you.

es.L: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:amen|amad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos y {{plural_you:oren|orad}} por los que {{plural_you:los|os}} persiguen,
es.B: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:amen|amad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos, y {{plural_you:oren|orad}} por la gente que {{plural_you:los|os}} persigue,
es.R: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:amen|amad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos. {{plural_you:Oren|Orad}} por quienes {{plural_you:les|os}} hacen daño.

fr.L: Mais moi, je vous dis : aimez vos ennemis et priez pour ceux qui vous persécutent,
fr.B: Mais moi, je vous le dis : aimez vos ennemis, et priez pour ceux qui vous persécutent,
fr.R: Mais moi, je vous le dis : aimez vos ennemis. Priez pour ceux qui vous font souffrir.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia, wapendeni maadui wenu, na kuwaombea wale wanaowatesa,
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia: wapendeni maadui wenu, na muwaombee watu wanaowatesa,
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia, wapendeni maadui wenu. Waombeeni watu wanaowaumiza.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 너희에게 말한다. 너희의 원수들을 사랑하고, 너희를 박해하는 사람들을 위하여 기도하여라.
ko.B: 그러나 나는 너희에게 말한다. 너희 원수를 사랑하여라. 그리고 너희를 박해하는 사람들을 위해 기도하여라.
ko.R: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 너희 원수를 사랑하여라. 너희를 괴롭히는 사람들을 위해 기도하여라.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con: hãy yêu thương kẻ thù của các con và cầu nguyện cho những người bắt bớ các con,
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con: hãy yêu thương kẻ thù mình và cầu nguyện cho những người bắt bớ các con,
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, hãy yêu thương kẻ thù của mình. Hãy cầu nguyện cho những người làm hại các con.

pt.L: Mas eu lhes digo: amem os inimigos de vocês e orem por aqueles que perseguem vocês,
pt.B: Mas eu lhes digo: amem os inimigos de vocês e orem por quem persegue vocês,
pt.R: Mas eu digo a vocês: amem quem é inimigo de vocês. Orem pelas pessoas que fazem mal a vocês.

am.L: እኔ ግን እላችኋለሁ፣ ጠላቶቻችሁን ውደዱ፤ ለሚያሳድዷችሁም ጸልዩ፣
am.B: እኔ ግን እላችኋለሁ፦ ጠላቶቻችሁን ውደዱ፤ ስለሚያሳድዷችሁም ሰዎች ጸልዩ፣
am.R: እኔ ግን እነግራችኋለሁ፣ ጠላቶቻችሁን ውደዱ። ለሚጎዷችሁ ሰዎች ጸልዩ።

ru.L: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю вам: любите ваших врагов и молитесь за преследующих вас,
ru.B: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю вам: любите своих врагов и молитесь за тех, кто вас преследует,
ru.R: Но {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю вам: любите своих врагов. Молитесь за тех, кто причиняет вам зло.

hi.L: पर मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ, अपने दुश्मनों से प्रेम करो और जो तुम्हें सताते हैं, उनके लिए प्रार्थना करो,
hi.B: पर मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ: अपने शत्रुओं से प्रेम करो, और उन लोगों के लिए प्रार्थना करो जो तुम्हें सताते हैं,
hi.R: पर मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ, अपने दुश्मनों से प्रेम करो। जो लोग तुम्हें दुःख देते हैं, उनके लिए प्रार्थना करो।

uk.L: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} кажу вам: любіть своїх ворогів і моліться за тих, хто вас переслідує,
uk.B: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} кажу вам: любіть своїх ворогів і моліться за тих, хто вас переслідує,
uk.R: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} кажу вам: любіть своїх ворогів. Моліться за людей, які вам шкодять.

ja.L: しかしこのわたしは、あなたがたに言う。あなたがたの敵を愛し、あなたがたを迫害する者たちのために祈りなさい。
ja.B: しかし、わたしがあなたがたに言うのは、こうである。あなたがたの敵を愛しなさい。あなたがたを迫害する人々のために祈りなさい。
ja.R: でも、わたしはあなたたちにこう言う。あなたたちの敵を愛しなさい。あなたたちを苦しめる人たちのために祈りなさい。

decisions.choice: love: seek their good, whatever you feel
decisions.reason: The command is to act for the good of enemies and to pray for them, as God does good to all (5:45).

decisions.choice: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: with "bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you" added, from Luke 6:27-28, in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts fill out the verse with words from Luke. Early manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.

records.literal_gloss: so that you may become sons of the Father of you the in heavens, because the sun of him he makes rise on evil and good and sends rain on righteous and unrighteous.

en.L: so that you may become {{gender:children|sons}} of your Father who [is] in [the] heavens, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sun rise on [the] evil and [the] good, and sends rain on [the] righteous and [the] unrighteous.
en.B: so that you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of your Father in heaven. He makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sun rise on evil people and good people alike, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends rain on those who do right and those who do wrong.
en.R: Then you will show that you are {{gender:children|sons}} of your Father in heaven. He makes the sun shine on bad people and good people. He sends rain to people who do right and to people who do wrong.

es.L: para que {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a ser hijos de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que [está] en [los] cielos, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace salir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sol sobre [los] malos y [los] buenos, y envía lluvia sobre [los] justos y [los] injustos.
es.B: para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} hijos de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo. Él hace que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sol salga sobre los malos y sobre los buenos por igual, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} envía la lluvia sobre los que hacen el bien y sobre los que hacen el mal.
es.R: Entonces {{plural_you:mostrarán|mostraréis}} que {{plural_you:son|sois}} hijos de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo. Él hace que el sol brille sobre la gente mala y sobre la gente buena. Envía la lluvia a los que hacen lo correcto y a los que hacen lo malo.

fr.L: afin que vous deveniez {{gender:enfants|fils}} de votre Père qui [est] dans les cieux, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait lever {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} soleil sur les méchants et sur les bons, et fait pleuvoir sur les justes et sur les injustes.
fr.B: Ainsi vous serez {{gender:enfants|fils}} de votre Père qui est dans les cieux. Il fait lever {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} soleil sur les méchants comme sur les bons, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait tomber la pluie sur ceux qui font le bien et sur ceux qui font le mal.
fr.R: Alors vous montrerez que vous êtes {{gender:enfants|fils}} de votre Père qui est dans le ciel. Il fait briller le soleil sur les gens mauvais et sur les gens bons. Il envoie la pluie sur ceux qui font le bien et sur ceux qui font le mal.

sw.L: ili muwe wana wa Baba yenu aliye katika mbingu, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hulifanya jua {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} lichomoze juu ya waovu na wema, na huleta mvua juu ya wenye haki na wasio na haki.
sw.B: ili muwe wana wa Baba yenu wa mbinguni. Yeye hulifanya jua {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} lichomoze juu ya watu waovu na watu wema pia, na hunyesha mvua juu ya wale wanaotenda haki na wale wanaotenda maovu.
sw.R: Hivyo mtaonyesha kwamba ninyi ni wana wa Baba yenu aliye mbinguni. Yeye hufanya jua liwaangazie watu wabaya na watu wema. Huwanyeshea mvua watu wanaotenda haki na watu wanaotenda mabaya.

ko.L: 그래야 너희가 하늘들에 계신 너희 아버지의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이 될 것이다. 그분은 자기 해를 악한 사람들과 선한 사람들 위에 떠오르게 하시고, 의로운 사람들과 불의한 사람들 위에 비를 내리시기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러면 너희는 하늘에 계신 너희 아버지의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이 될 것이다. 아버지께서는 악한 사람에게나 선한 사람에게나 똑같이 해를 떠오르게 하시고, 의로운 사람에게나 불의한 사람에게나 비를 내려 주신다.
ko.R: 그러면 너희가 하늘에 계신 너희 아버지의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이라는 것을 보여 주게 될 것이다. 아버지께서는 나쁜 사람에게도 좋은 사람에게도 해를 비추어 주신다. 옳은 일을 하는 사람에게도, 잘못된 일을 하는 사람에게도 비를 내려 주신다.

vi.L: để các con trở nên con cái của Cha các con, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khiến mặt trời của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mọc lên trên kẻ ác và người thiện, và cho mưa xuống trên người công chính và kẻ bất chính.
vi.B: để các con trở nên con cái của Cha các con ở trên trời. Ngài cho mặt trời của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mọc lên trên người ác cũng như người tốt, và cho mưa xuống trên người làm điều đúng lẫn người làm điều sai.
vi.R: Như vậy các con sẽ cho thấy mình là con cái của Cha các con ở trên trời. Ngài làm cho mặt trời chiếu sáng trên người xấu lẫn người tốt. Ngài cho mưa xuống trên người làm điều đúng lẫn người làm điều sai.

pt.L: para que vocês se tornem filhos do Pai de vocês que [está] nos céus, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} sol nascer sobre maus e bons e faz chover sobre justos e injustos.

decisions.choice: become sons of your Father: be like him, and so show you are his children
alternatives: earn the right to be his children
decisions.reason: A son was expected to be like his father. Those who love their enemies act as God does, and so show the family likeness (5:9).

decisions.choice: his sun and his rain for all: God's kindness to good and bad alike
decisions.reason: God gives the gifts of life to everyone, including those who oppose him. His children are to love in the same way.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: As in 5:9.

decisions.choice: you will show that you are
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "become" here: being seen to be what they are.

decisions.choice: hijos, no setting
decisions.reason: Where the English offers "children" with "sons" as the traditional form, Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, as in Romans 8:14, so it carries no gender span.

decisions.choice: {{gender:enfants|fils}} without an article
decisions.reason: As in Luke 6:35. With no article French reads "enfants de votre Père" as a status, which is the sense of being like him (m1).

decisions.choice: wana, no setting
decisions.reason: "Wana" is used of sons and daughters alike, as in Romans 8:14, so the English gender setting has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: {{gender:자녀|아들}}들
decisions.reason: As in 5:9: the Greek "sons" means all God's children, and Korean has two ways of saying it; the plural ending stands outside the span.

decisions.choice: "con cái" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in 5:9: "con cái" is how Vietnamese says children of a father, and "con trai" would not serve as a traditional alternative with the same sense.

decisions.choice: filhos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: As in 5:9: Portuguese "filhos" already means sons and daughters together, so the English setting is not needed.

decisions.choice: የአባታችሁ ልጆች (children of your Father), with no gender or deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: "ልጆች" is the ordinary Amharic plural for what the Greek means here, so the gender setting has no second wording; and the Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so pronouns for God are written plainly.

decisions.choice: {{gender:सन्तान|पुत्र}}
decisions.reason: Hindi has two real ways to say this: "सन्तान" (children, of either sex) and "पुत्र" (sons). The default says whom Jesus means; the alternative keeps the Greek's "sons". "की" before the span is the postposition of "पिता की", which fits both.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span
alternatives: a span offering a capitalised pronoun
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. The honorific "वे", "उगाते हैं" for God carries the respect at every level.

decisions.choice: 'своему солнцу' without a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Russian says 'his own' with the reflexive 'свой', which takes no deity_pronoun span, where the English has one on 'his'.

decisions.choice: "子ら" (L); "子ども" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in 5:9: Japanese 子 already includes daughters and sons.

decisions.choice: "세리들" at every level

decisions.choice: os cobradores de impostos
decisions.reason: For the whole book (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6): "publicano" is a church word most readers do not know; "cobradores de impostos" says what they did, at every level.

decisions.choice: ቀራጮች (tax collectors)

decisions.choice: perfect: complete, whole, undivided, here above all in love
decisions.reason: The word means complete or whole. After 5:43-47 it means love that is whole, like God's, which leaves no one out. It echoes "You shall be holy, for I am holy" (Leviticus 19:2) and "You shall be blameless" (Deuteronomy 18:13).

decisions.choice: you shall be: a command in the form of a future
decisions.reason: As often in the law, the future tense gives a command.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} (L); {{plural_you:han de ser|habéis de ser}} (B); {{plural_you:tienen que ser|tenéis que ser}} (R)
decisions.reason: The future is a command (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the future; Balanced says "haber de", which is both a duty and what will be; Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: mtakuwa (L); mnapaswa kuwa (B); lazima muwe (R)
decisions.reason: The future is a command (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the future; Balanced and Readable say it as a duty.

decisions.choice: "온전하다" (L, B); "완전하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The footnoted meaning decision reads the word as complete, whole, undivided; "온전" has that sense of wholeness, where "완전" can sound like flawlessness. Readable uses the more everyday word.

decisions.choice: the comparison after the main clause in Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, command first and the comparison after it; Balanced and Readable put the comparison first, as Korean normally does.

decisions.choice: "trọn vẹn" for perfect
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as complete, whole and undivided, above all in love; "trọn vẹn" says wholeness, while "hoàn hảo" suggests being without any flaw.

decisions.choice: "Cha trên trời của các con" (L)
alternatives: "Cha các con, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời"
decisions.reason: Here the Greek has the adjective "heavenly", not "in the heavens" (5:16, 5:45), so Literal does not use the plural phrase.

decisions.choice: "सिद्ध"
decisions.reason: "सिद्ध" means complete and whole, the sense of the Greek, without suggesting someone who never makes a mistake.

decisions.choice: "完全な者となる[べきである]"
decisions.reason: The Greek future gives a command, as often in the law (m2). Literal keeps the future and shows the command in brackets; Balanced and Readable say it as a command.
